svg.title: Fadecandy system overview: one Raspberry Pi, one Fadecandy, eight LED runs, one 5 V supply
svg.desc: The Raspberry Pi 3B+ connects to a Fadecandy board over USB. Each of the Fadecandy's eight channels leaves the board as a pair: a yellow DATA wire to the DI pad of one 64-pixel WS2812B run, and a black GND wire from that same channel's minus pin, twisted with it and landed on the GND bus alongside that run's own ground lead. There are eight such pairs, not eight lone data wires. The 5 V power supply feeds a red +5 V bus and a black GND bus that power the runs directly, and each run takes its +5 V off that bus through its own 5 A branch fuse. Strip current flows only between the supply and the runs; it never passes through the Fadecandy or the Pi.
svg.text: Diagram 1 - System overview: one control point, eight runs
Strip current flows only between the 5 V supply and the runs. It never passes through the Fadecandy or the Pi.
8 × DATA - one yellow wire per Fadecandy channel, ch 0 … ch 7
8 × GND - one black wire per channel, twisted with its DATA. Mandatory.
Android app talks to it over Wi-Fi / LAN
its own 5 V PSU - not the LED supply
Open-frame: MUST be enclosed and earthed.
Set output to 5.00 V with a meter - see § Safety.
V+ → +5 V bus V− → GND bus
Mains in on the far side, behind a barrier.
The Fadecandy carries no strip current.
Its J2 header has GND and DATA pins only - there is no
+5 V pin on it. Strip current leaves the supply's V+, goes
through the LEDs, and returns to the supply's V−.
Why the ground tie is mandatory
The DATA signal is a voltage measured against ground. The
Fadecandy drives it against ITS ground; each WS2812B reads
it against the SUPPLY's ground. If those two grounds are not
bonded, the LEDs have no reference, and the run will show
nothing, flicker, or display garbage colours.
Data and ground always travel together. Always.
